rows: Its plaster-like finish makes models look like traditional castings—with a natural, matte texture and clear reproduction of even the finest details.

Thanks to its high print resolution and dimensional stability, PLA MINERAL is an excellent choice for architectural, artistic, and model-making studios, as well as for all applications requiring faithful detail reproduction—from scale models and sculptures to precision prototypes. The material allows for aesthetic finishes: prints can be further processed, such as sanding or staining, which provides great freedom in creating a final effect reminiscent of a traditional plaster cast.
Maker statement only; no application validation, exposure test or suitability established. Specific conditions not published.

polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. NatureWorks Ingeo 3D850 (R-NATUREWORKS-INGEO-3D850-TDS), a PLA grade for 3D-printing monofilament, prints a specific gravity of 1.24 (ASTM D792), a peak melt temperature of 165-180 °C and a glass transition temperature of 55-60 °C (both ASTM D3418), p. 1. It prints no water absorption. PLA is semicrystalline and prints amorphous (D158): the melting point column holds 165 °C, the low end of the printed range, a ceiling every grade of the range stays under. The same page says that annealing "in the range of 176-266°F (80-130°C) can be used to promote crystallization": the annealing threshold is the glass transition's low end, 55 °C, at or below which nothing crystallises (D158).

Of the solvents studied, chloroform is the best solvent for quickly preparing 10 % wt/vol solutions of all Ingeo grades and morphologies; 4032D pellets and injection-moulded bars were readily transformed to 10 % wt/vol solutions in chloroform in 2-4 hours at room temperature

Study grades: 4060D (12 % D, amorphous), 2003D (4.5 % D) and 4032D (1.6 % D, crystallisable) as pellets and injection-moulded bars; no filament grade was tested.
